labelChirho: from here, away from this place
descriptionChirho: Adverb of spatial origin indicating motion or departure from the speaker's location, meaning 'from here, from this place.' Used in contexts such as Jesus telling others to depart (John 2:16, 7:3, 14:31, 18:36; Matt 17:20; Luke 4:9, 13:31, 16:26). Translations uniformly indicate directional origin: Spanish 'de aquí,' Hindi 'यहाँ–से/यहां–से,' Arabic 'مِنْ هُنَا,' Korean '여기서/여기–에서,' Swahili 'kutoka hapa.' This is the primary and most frequent usage of the adverb.

labelChirho: on this side, on one side
descriptionChirho: Adverb of spatial position meaning 'on this side' or 'on that side,' used distributively in the phrase 'on this side... and on that side' (ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ἐντεῦθεν) to indicate positioning on both flanks or sides of something (John 19:18, Rev 22:2). This sense is genuinely distinct from the directional 'from here' because it denotes static spatial arrangement rather than motion. Spanish 'de un lado/de otro lado,' Hindi 'इस–तरफ/उस–तरफ,' Korean '이쪽–에/저쪽–에,' Swahili 'upande huu' all support the 'on this/that side' reading rather than 'from here.'
